messages:
mia_support: FYI incoming high-severity from Acme. Customer reports streaming completions arriving with partial payloads, duplicate chunks, and sometimes chunks arriving out of order when requests traverse our gRPC gateway + external proxy chain. Logs attached from their side.

acme_cust_john: Hi team — this started after we routed traffic through our edge proxy for A/B testing. We see repeated tokens and gibberish mid-stream, then client reconnects and gets the rest but order is wrong. Billing shows two requests charged for one user action. 

mia_support: Repro notes they gave: model endpoint /v1/streams/generate (gpt-like) using SSE. Client is Chrome fetch to our hosted API behind an nginx -> envoy -> redwood-gateway chain. They included curl reproducer: 
```bash
curl -v --http2 -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \\\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \\\n  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/generate?model=redwood-7b"
```

jon_eng-runtime: Can you paste one of the raw SSE sessions (client view) and any request/response headers? suspect chunk re-framing at an intermediary.

acme_cust_john: pasted snippet below (client side):
```
data: {"token":"The quick brown"}\n\n

data: {"token":" fox jumps"}\n\n

data: {"token":" over the"}\n\n

data: {"token":" lazy dog"}\n\n\n# then reconnect\
data: {"token":" fox jumps"}\n\n

data: {"token":"The quick brown"}\n\n

data: {"token":" over the"}\n```

mia_support: Looks like chunk duplication and order inversion on reconnect. Also billing double-charge on reconnect.

selina_eng-platform: Two likely failure modes: 1) intermediary (nginx/envoy) re-chunking/ buffering when converting between HTTP/2 and HTTP/1.1 and 2) gRPC gateway doing a buffered translate that doesn't preserve SSE event boundaries. Both can cause reordering when partial stream resumes.

jon_eng-runtime: Agreed. Runtime uses chunked flush boundaries that map to SSE events. If an intermediary merges/splits TCP segments and then a TCP reset/reconnect happens, the client may replay with Last-Event-ID and server may replay some buffered tokens. We should look for missing X-Request-Id and streaming UUIDs.

acme_cust_john: We do send Last-Event-ID on reconnect sometimes, but the reconnect comes from the browser after a 502. The gateway logs show a 502 and then a new connection, same session id but new request id.

mia_support: Can you enable X-Redwood-Stream-Id and show gateway logs for the failing window? Also capture tcpdump or h2dump for a sample.

acme_cust_john: attaching a gateway dump and nginx config excerpt. nginx has proxy_buffering on by default.

mia_support: nginx proxy_buffering is a red flag for SSE. If proxy_buffering is on it will coalesce chunks. Suggest set `proxy_buffering off; proxy_buffer_size 4k;` for SSE routes.

jon_eng-runtime: Also see this pattern: gRPC-gateway (h2 -> h1) will translate trailers poorly if it tries to buffer response until content-length/tail available. For streaming we should ensure streaming=true passthrough mode.

selina_eng-platform: Repro steps we should run:
1) Hit the endpoint from a client using direct connection to runtime (bypass gateway) with `--http2` curl reproducer to confirm behavior.
2) Replay through nginx+envoy+gateway chain.
3) Capture `nginx -T` and envoy config and run `h2dump` on the wire.
4) Compare SSE event boundaries and X-Request-Id / X-Redwood-Stream-Id.

jon_eng-runtime: Workaround for customer while we investigate:
- Ask them to disable proxy_buffering for the SSE route and enable `chunked_transfer_encoding on;` in nginx.
- On the client, reconnect using Last-Event-ID and send `X-Redwood-Stream-Id` header so server can dedupe repeated tokens.

luke_cs: Customer is asking for a hotfix we can suggest to prevent double billing. Any quick server-side dedupe we can enable?

jon_eng-runtime: We can add a short-lived idempotency window keyed by Stream-Id + event-sequence to avoid billing on replay within N secs. Short term patch: if reconnect is detected within 60s and stream id matches, don't increment billing counters for events with duplicate sequence numbers. This requires customer to send stream id on reconnect.

mia_support: Acme said they cannot modify client quickly. They want Redwood to handle it. Is it safe to enable dedupe server-side without client changes?

jon_eng-runtime: We can try heuristics (same client ip + last request id + small time window) but not bulletproof. Prefer explicit Stream-Id.

selina_eng-platform: Immediate triage plan:
- Jon: investigate runtime SSE flush boundaries + add logging to include `X-Redwood-Stream-Id` and per-event seq. Capture a failing trace.
- Infra: ask Acme to run `curl --http2` bypassing nginx; we'll compare.
- CS: request tcpdump/h2dump/gateway logs and confirm sample request ids.
- Support: provide nginx config snippets for SSE.

jon_eng-runtime: Adding repro command for team:
```bash
# direct to runtime (bypass gateway)
curl -v --http2 -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \\\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\\n  -H "X-Redwood-Stream-Id: test-stream-123" \\\n  "https://runtime.internal/v1/streams/generate?model=redwood-7b"

# through gateway chain (nginx -> envoy -> gateway)
curl -v --http2 -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \\\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\\n  -H "X-Redwood-Stream-Id: test-stream-123" \\\n  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/generate?model=redwood-7b"
```

acme_cust_john: Ran direct test — no duplication when bypassing nginx. Through chain we reproduce ~70% of the time. We changed nginx proxy_buffering off and it reduced errors but didn't eliminate them.

jon_eng-runtime: That isolates nginx as a contributor. Envoy might also be buffering for h2->h1 transform. Check envoy cluster config stream idle timeouts and `enable_http1_streaming` option.

mia_support: I've created an internal ticket and attached customer logs + gateway dump. Ticket #INC-2026-814. Assigned to jon_eng-runtime and selina_eng-platform.

infra_bot: Incident created INC-2026-814 by mia_support. Priority: P2.

selina_eng-platform: Next steps for platform team: audit gRPC gateway translation layer for SSE passthrough flag and test with conn reset during mid-event boundary. If buffering detected, add explicit pass-through toggle for SSE routes.

jon_eng-runtime: I'll instrument per-event seq headers and add optional dedupe window. Will post a canary tomorrow.

luke_cs: I'll update customer with diagnostics and recommended nginx specific config (disable proxy_buffering, set chunked_transfer_encoding on, add keepalive tweaks) and offer dedicated routing to bypass their edge proxy while we patch.

acme_cust_john: Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround. We'll try the nginx tweaks and confirm.

mia_support: Great. If anyone reproduces locally, paste minimal h2dump + a small sample of the swapped chunks. We want one canonical repro to attach to the runtime PR.

jon_eng-runtime: Will do. I expect a small runtime patch and a configuration doc to prevent this class of issue.

mia_support: Closing this thread when we have canary results. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
